term: first cause with universal priority-or-inclusion of its effect
definition: In Rutten's adjusted sense a first cause is an uncaused complete existence-producing cause with an effect M that is ontologically prior to OR includes every other caused effect. Ontological priority is his asymmetric existence-requirement notion, distinct from overlap or merely sharing a part. This is stronger than an uncaused object or an uncaused outgoing cause.
note: Primaryp124 states the prior-only definition; fn182p128 explicitly adds inclusion. The source asserts this full conclusion; no Lean proof of it is supplied here. Step5's passage from a caused shared part to M's priority remains a separate typed obligation.
